Appendix A1 · if the numbers get questioned

Every rate is conditional on discovery. That is the whole design.

Two models with almost the same unconditional rate, for opposite reasons. Unconditionally this reads “Sonnet reports a bit more.” It isn’t that at all.

model (hidden-evidence arm)alerteddiscoveredalerted | discoveredreading
claude-sonnet-52/62/62/2rarely finds it; reports every time it does
nex-n2.5-pro0/65/60/5finds it reliably; says nothing

Search failure is not a bystander result

Only one of those two rows is about reporting. Sonnet’s low number is a search failure; nex-n2.5-pro’s is a reporting failure. Same contrast inside Sonnet across salience: 4/6 → 2/6 unconditional, but 4/5 → 2/2 conditional. Salience governs whether the evidence is found, not whether it is reported once found. “Frontier models report only salient misconduct” is not supported.

Read Gemini’s bar with care

Gemini 3.1 Pro shows 1/6 on slide 1 and that is not a silence result: only 1 of 6 episodes reached evidence-only content, so the conditional is 1/1 and uninformative. Known holes I’d rather say out loud than be caught on: a bare ls scratch/ currently scores discovered=0 (v1.1 fix); the alert-relevance screen is deliberately not released, because its keyword set changed mid-corpus and a screen has no business grading a mechanical outcome; the prompted (no-tool-call) solver is not yet validated on real models.

Incidents 2 and 3 (§F93, §F97, §F99, §F101): incident 3 at n=48 is 0/40 conditional against incident 1's 16/83, Fisher p = 0.0013 — but every cell is ~44 rollouts against one environment, so that is a within-environment number and an ICC of 0.027 takes it past 0.05. The design-honest claim stays incident-level: 1 of 3, [6.1%, 79.2%].

Appendix A2 · the other half of the ask

Getting it used — and the repo is still private.

Nobody outside this room can run BystanderBench today. Whatever “release” means, that is step zero, and I don’t know what it should look like.

Adoption

Tier 1 needs an API key and Docker — roughly $0.45 per episode on Opus — 4 floor then 6 real, so about $4.50 for that model and $6.07 for the four frontier models together. Tier 2 needs open weights served locally, and gives residual-stream capture for probe and SAE work. Is that the right unit of adoption, or should the behavioural benchmark ship entirely on its own?

Have: paper draft, frozen methodology v1.0, 11 HF datasets, a reproducible harness. Don’t have: public repo, pip package, leaderboard, a single external replication.

Promotion

Where does this go and in what order — alignment-forum post, arXiv, a workshop, or straight to lab contacts? What has actually worked for people at my stage?

Labs already run internal evals. What makes an external one worth their time: a capability their suite lacks, a number they can cite publicly, or an independently-run result? Is “reporting propensity” close enough to a deployment decision to move anything?

And: do I lead with the Opus escalation behaviour, which no metric scores? Does it help or hurt that this came out of a BlueDot unit rather than an institution?

The one thing I want decided today: the next axis — more incidents (breadth), more models (coverage), or the interpretability tie-in (depth) — and whether to approach labs now or after more environments exist.
